applyd-hub.short: A career document and application manager that ends tailoring fatigue for job and scholarship seekers.
applyd-hub.problem: Every job or scholarship application means rewriting your CV from scratch. I was facing this myself.
applyd-hub.role: Solo: product, design, mobile, backend, launch and marketing.
approach: Built it for my own applications first. When I showed it to a few people, they wanted it too, so I turned it into a product.
One profile works as the single source of truth, and tailored documents are generated from it.
Instead of starting over, the AI improves a document step by step.
Tracks each job and scholarship from saved to offer, with a compatibility score before you apply.
applyd-hub.result: Live on the App Store and Google Play, with 30+ downloads and growing.

propatis.short: A comprehensive real estate platform that simplifies property management and tenant interactions for businesses and individuals.
propatis.problem: Real estate businesses run properties, tenants and requests across scattered tools, and their listings live on separate sites.
propatis.role: Founding engineer and product lead: I lead a team of 4, set the roadmap and assign the work.
approach: Built the mobile app by myself, and build the web app with the team.
User feedback showed both the B2B and B2C experiences were hard to use, so I'm redesigning the UI: the landing page is done, B2B is next, then B2C.
Ran paid campaigns, set up analytics to see where users come from, and pitched and onboarded clients one on one.
One platform covers three sides: management for businesses, listings on their own websites, and a public marketplace.
propatis.result: ~200 daily visitors. The new landing page is done, and the mobile app is awaiting App Store and Google Play approval.

perry-luscious.short: A website for a Lyon-based bakery to showcase its cakes and take customer orders, with a 3D cake designer built in Three.js.
perry-luscious.problem: A Lyon pâtisserie took orders through social media messages, which meant a lot of back and forth over designs, details and delivery.
perry-luscious.role: Freelance: product thinking, design, build, SEO and analytics.
approach: Designed ordering around how she works: customers pick a design, customise it and set delivery in one flow, so orders arrive complete.
Built a 3D cake designer with Three.js, so customers can see their cake before they order.
Kept the path from browsing to checkout deliberately short, with her creations shown so customers see what to expect.
Built a French and English site the owner can update herself through Sanity.
Added SEO, plus Google Tag Manager connected to TikTok and Instagram, so she can see which channel brings customers and put her effort there.
perry-luscious.result: Around 80% of her orders, about 20 a month, now come through the website, with far less back and forth.

testimonial.quote: The website is very seamless. Customers can put in every detail they want and customise their order, and see their choices without asking lots of questions. It gave my business a premium look, helped me keep customers and brought in new ones.
testimonial.name: Perry, owner of Perry Luscious

lab-brain.short: An open-source research workspace that links samples, characterization, analysis and conclusions for materials science.
lab-brain.problem: Research data ends up scattered across folders, spreadsheets, slides and notes, so results can't be traced back to the sample that produced them.
lab-brain.role: Solo, built for my own PhD research.
approach: I had a Python workflow in VS Code. When a labmate asked me about my analysis, I realised the same tools could help people who don't code, so I built a UI on top.
It links sample, characterization, analysis and conclusion, so the next researcher can pick up my work and my supervisor can follow my progress easily.
Runs characterization calculations and plots (EDX, ellipsometry, FTIR), with an AI assistant that answers from your own records.
lab-brain.result: I use it several times a week to log and analyse my experiments.
